\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Tableau size bound]
\lean{Complexity.tableau_size_le}
\label{Complexity.tableau_size_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For all natural numbers $W,c,C,d,n$,
$$n+2+\bigl(c\bigl((C+1)(n+1)^{d+1}+1\bigr)^2+1\bigr)W\leq
(2+W+c(C+2)^2W)(n+1)^{2(d+1)}.$$
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time has polynomial-size circuits]
\lean{Complexity.P_subset_PPoly}
\label{Complexity.P_subset_PPoly}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.mem_language_iff, BoolCircuit.PPoly, Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Complexity.oblivious_of_mem_DTIME, Complexity.tableauCircuit, Complexity.tableauCircuit_eval_of_decidesInTime, Complexity.tableauCircuit_isFaninTwo, Complexity.tableauCircuit_size, Complexity.tableauWidth, Complexity.tableau_size_le, Complexity.timeConstructible_poly, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{5}
Every binary language decidable in polynomial time has a family of Boolean circuits with
fan-in at most two that decides it, with constants $a,k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the
circuit for inputs of length $n$ has size at most $a(n+1)^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time and polynomial-size circuits]
\lean{Complexity.P_ne_NP_of_not_NP_subset_PPoly}
\label{Complexity.P_ne_NP_of_not_NP_subset_PPoly}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.PPoly, Complexity.NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.P_subset_PPoly}
\difficulty{1}
If there is a language in $\mathsf{NP}$ that is not decidable by any family of Boolean
circuits of fan-in at most two whose size is bounded by a polynomial, then $\mathsf{P}
\ne \mathsf{NP}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time and polynomial-size circuits]
\lean{Complexity.P_ssubset_PPoly}
\label{Complexity.P_ssubset_PPoly}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.PPoly, Complexity.P, Complexity.P_ssubset_PPoly_of_subset, Complexity.P_subset_PPoly}
\difficulty{1}
The class $\mathsf{P}$ of polynomial-time decidable binary languages is a proper subset
of the class of languages decided by polynomial-size Boolean circuit families with
fan-in at most two.
\end{theorem}
